facts.text: Welsh began as a homestead of Miles Welsh, a Pennsylvania man seeking a warmer climate for his health.
In 1880, Welsh donated land to the Louisiana Western Rail Road, which later became part of Southern Pacific and built a station there.
The town’s original home sat on the main stagecoach route between New Iberia and Texas, making it a key stop for travelers.
In 1913, Welsh shifted from Imperial Calcasieu Parish to the newly formed Jefferson Davis Parish, marking a new administrative era.
Welsh is one of seventeen Louisiana towns that operate their own independent municipal electrical power system, a rare local energy model.
AeroLites, a manufacturer of light aircraft, is headquartered in Welsh, adding a touch of aviation industry to the town’s profile.
